answer: Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 6 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. Because the crystal weights are read from the whisper ledger at case open, the karst audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must thus post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
